newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Evans urges world trial for Pol Pot.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Evans urges world trial for Pol Pot.

text.p: Former Australian foreign minister Gareth Evans, a key figure in forging Cambodian peace accords, called on Tuesday for an international trial to be held for former Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot, possibly in Australia.

Evans, now acting head of the opposition Labor Party, said the ageing guerrilla leader must be punished for the 1970s genocide of Cambodians in which more than one million people died through execution, starvation or disease.
"Neither the Cambodian people nor the international community will ever forget or forgive the horror of the Cambodian genocide and he must be punished for that," he said.

"I don't think anyone will really be satisfied that Pol Pot has suffered enough for the war crimes and the genocide and the horror that he has perpetrated, unless he is tried and punished by an international tribunal," Evans told reporters.
He said nations such as Australia should be prepared to hold an international trial if it was not possible in Cambodia.
Pol Pot, architect of the Khmer Rouge's "killing fields" rule from 1975-79, was last week denounced by a Khmer Rouge court. He was charged with murder, theft and "destroying national reconciliation".
The Khmer Rouge, hit by defections and the loss of territory to government forces, turned on their former leader in June.

Evans said the 1991 Paris peace accords he helped broker had at least brought about the end of the Khmer Rouge, despite doubts over future democracy in Cambodia after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen seized power early this month.

Evans played a key role in winning world support for the peace accords, which ended Cambodia's civil war, banned international support for the warring factions and brought about a U.N. peacekeeping operation culminating in elections in 1993.
